head.citation-title: Rapid carbonation of recycled cement paste powder (RCPP) by amino acid-based carbamate solution: Preliminary study on phase assemblage and microstructure of carbonated product
head.abstracts: Copyright © 2026. Published by Elsevier Ltd.Conventional accelerated carbonation suffers from low CO2 utilization efficiency, spatiotemporal constraints, and high equipment requirements. To overcome these limitations, this study introduced a novel wet carbonation method using a CO2-loaded amino acid salt (AAS) solution, specifically an amino acid (AA)-based carbamate solution, for treating recycled cement paste powder (RCPP). The process produced abundant spherical and cubic CaCO3 particles (1—2 μm) on RCPP surfaces. Polycrystalline analysis showed vaterite dominated within 30 min under serine (Ser) regulation, while the arginine (Arg)-based system produced over 50 % calcite. After 30-min immersion, the total CaCO3 content stabilized, accounting for 48.4 %—51.5 % and 42.6 %—46.7 % of the carbonated RCPP mass in the Ser- and Arg-based groups, respectively. Arg’s weaker crystalline control further facilitated the transformation of metastable vaterite into more stable polymorphs over time. Incorporating 30 % carbonated RCPP enhanced compressive strength by 5.4 %—21.9 %, attributed to micro-/nano-CaCO3 promoting cement hydration and refining microstructure. The recovered filtrate maintained 88.46 %—95.64 % of its initial CO2 absorption capacity. After four absorption-utilization cycles, Ser- and Arg-based filtrates retained 78.93 % and 56.16 % of initial CO2 loading. Although accompanied by 11.3 % and 9.1 % reductions in CaCO3 content, compressive strength experienced only marginal declines, ranging from -0.1—6.60 %. This innovative approach provides dual environmental benefits by enabling efficient CO2 sequestration and promoting resource utilization of RCPP.

coredata.dc:description: Conventional accelerated carbonation suffers from low CO2 utilization efficiency, spatiotemporal constraints, and high equipment requirements. To overcome these limitations, this study introduced a novel wet carbonation method using a CO2-loaded amino acid salt (AAS) solution, specifically an amino acid (AA)-based carbamate solution, for treating recycled cement paste powder (RCPP). The process produced abundant spherical and cubic CaCO3 particles (1—2 μm) on RCPP surfaces. Polycrystalline analysis showed vaterite dominated within 30 min under serine (Ser) regulation, while the arginine (Arg)-based system produced over 50 % calcite. After 30-min immersion, the total CaCO3 content stabilized, accounting for 48.4 %—51.5 % and 42.6 %—46.7 % of the carbonated RCPP mass in the Ser- and Arg-based groups, respectively. Arg’s weaker crystalline control further facilitated the transformation of metastable vaterite into more stable polymorphs over time. Incorporating 30 % carbonated RCPP enhanced compressive strength by 5.4 %—21.9 %, attributed to micro-/nano-CaCO3 promoting cement hydration and refining microstructure. The recovered filtrate maintained 88.46 %—95.64 % of its initial CO2 absorption capacity. After four absorption-utilization cycles, Ser- and Arg-based filtrates retained 78.93 % and 56.16 % of initial CO2 loading. Although accompanied by 11.3 % and 9.1 % reductions in CaCO3 content, compressive strength experienced only marginal declines, ranging from -0.1—6.60 %. This innovative approach provides dual environmental benefits by enabling efficient CO2 sequestration and promoting resource utilization of RCPP.
coredata.dc:title: Rapid carbonation of recycled cement paste powder (RCPP) by amino acid-based carbamate solution: Preliminary study on phase assemblage and microstructure of carbonated product
